land.text: 'In the 13th century Great Zimbabwe was on the fringe of the Mapungubwe state'; 'Around 1300, Great Zimbabwe replaced Mapungubwe as the most important trading centre in the interior'

predecessors.note: Political and cultural predecessor, not a territorial one: Great Zimbabwe lay on the fringe of Mapungubwe and did not take over its abandoned basin.

land.text: 'The state was composed of over 150 smaller zimbabwes, and likely covered 50,000 km2' (a 126 km disc around Great Zimbabwe has the same area)

successors.note: The Butua page says traditions collected in 1922 gave the kingdom 'the territory from Great Zimbabwe to the Makgadikgadi Pan'; the GZ page says 'By the 16th century, the Mutapa Empire and the Kingdom of Butua centred on Khami had replaced Great Zimbabwe as the major powers'. The Mutapa lineage also traces to Great Zimbabwe (Nyatsimba Mutota 'leaves to establish the Kingdom of Mutapa') but on the northern plateau, outside this disc.

capitals.name: Great Zimbabwe
capitals.note: Gazetteer point. 'Its capital was Great Zimbabwe, the largest stone structure in precolonial Southern Africa'; the page gives no capital dates, so the span is the state's span. 'Khami and Danamombe' are named only as 'later capitals'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Great Zimbabwe). The text gives 'likely covered 50,000 km2' with no year and no edges; drawn as a disc of that area around the capital (confidence 1 for the outline). The page also says it 'taxed other rulers throughout the region' and traded 'as far north as the Kundelungu Plateau', a tributary and trade reach that is not drawn.

ledger.note: c. 1250: Great Zimbabwe, a Shona stone-built capital, is a leading trade centre of the plateau. 'By 1250 Great Zimbabwe had become an important trade centre'; the infobox says 'Established: 13th century' and the page gives no single founding year or founder.

ledger.note: c. 1450: the Great Zimbabwe core passes to the Butua kingdom as the capital is deserted. The page is silent on a date and on who took the land: it gives 'From the early 15th century, international trade began to decline' and 'By the 16th century, political and economic power had shifted away from Great Zimbabwe to the north and west'; the Butua page (c. 1425 founding, traditions of a realm 'from Great Zimbabwe to the Makgadikgadi Pan') is the only hint of the holder.

region.text: 'The state was composed of over 150 smaller zimbabwes, and likely covered 50,000 km2' (a 126 km disc around Great Zimbabwe has the same area)

ledger.note: c. 1450: Great Zimbabwe ceases to be the seat of a kingdom, although the page says it 'likely continued to be inhabited into the 17th century'. The year 1450 is the researcher's bridge: the page gives only 'decline and migration of the Shona to other places from the 15th century' and the infobox '13th century-16th/17th century'.

certainty.note: No frontier is described; the realm was a tributary and trade network of over 150 smaller zimbabwes.

notes: Cliopatria has no Great Zimbabwe. Budget: one page (the state's article). Dates are the weakest of the batch: the page gives no founding year, no founder and no end year, only 'By 1250 ... an important trade centre', 'Around 1300 ... replaced Mapungubwe', decline 'from the early 15th century', and infobox bounds '13th century' and '16th/17th century'. The dossier runs 1250-1450: 1250 is the one year the page gives for the rise; 1450 is a bridging choice (confidence 1) that sits after the Butua founding (c. 1425, Butua page) and the first Mutapa activity. Area: 50,000 km2 (undated) drawn as a 126 km disc; the 7.22 km2 city figure is not territory. The Mutapa page says some Karanga from Great Zimbabwe migrated to the northern plateau in the 14th-15th centuries (Beach and Pikirayi) and Mutapa's founder is Nyatsimba Mutota only 'according to tradition'. Gazetteer: all names resolve (place Great Zimbabwe).
